headline: All majors below the 200-day line, momentum rolling over, but whales and stablecoin reserves signal mixed conviction.
paragraphs: The regime is unambiguous: every major asset in the board sits below its 200-day moving average, and no golden cross has formed to suggest a reversal. Bitcoin is at 63,653, down 49 percent from its 12-month high of 124,773, while Ethereum has fallen 60.6 percent from 4,829 to 1,905. Solana sits even deeper in the hole, down 70.4 percent to 73.25 from 247.56. The only minor relief comes from Bitcoin dominance holding firm at 56.6 percent, a sign that capital is consolidating into the largest asset rather than abandoning the space entirely. That said, total market cap rose 1.35 percent in the last 24 hours, a flicker of movement in a market that is structurally depressed below its long-term trend.

Momentum across the board is soft and diverging from the downtrend in ways that matter. Bitcoin's RSI sits at 47.4, neutral neither overbought nor oversold, while its MACD has rolled below the signal line, a sign that downward momentum is still present but losing urgency. Ethereum at 56.3 RSI looks slightly better but also carries a bearish MACD cross. The real outlier is positioning in BNB and DOGE: both trade below their 200-day lines yet both show MACD above the signal line, suggesting an uptick in momentum even as price remains underwater. This divergence, when paired with the broad soft RSI readings across the majors (Solana at 42.7, XRP at 42.9, ADA at 46.1), tells a tape that is resting rather than rolling over hard. Capitulation has not taken hold; the floor is not collapsing. The question is whether that rest becomes a spring or just a pause.

Derivatives positioning reveals heavy long bias and active liquidations of short sellers. Bitcoin's long-to-short ratio stands at 1.27 and has attracted 2 billion dollars in open interest at OKX. Funding is positive at 0.81 basis points per 8 hours, or 8.8 percent annualized, meaning longs are paying shorts to hold the trade. That is not expensive by historical standards but signals that the crowd is still willing to lever up on the belief that price goes higher. The real tension sits in liquidations: over the last 22 to 23 hours, shorts are taking the damage. Bitcoin liquidations have flushed 3.7 million dollars in short positions against only 584 thousand in longs. Ethereum shows 4.8 million in short liquidations against 1.46 million in longs. Solana and XRP repeat the pattern. This flow tells you that shorts have been caught off guard on rallies into an otherwise bearish setup, and that leverage is skewed toward bulls holding the line. If the tape breaks below key support, those long positions become fragile.

Whale flows paint a picture of mixed sentiment: Bitcoin saw 193 million dollars flow onto Kraken in the last 24 hours, but 80 million dollars left Binance, resulting in a net inflow of 112 million. More striking is the stablecoin movement: 187 million dollars in USDT moved onto OKEx and 119 million onto Bitfinex, while 127 million USDT left Bitfinex. The stablecoin float sits at 304.5 billion dollars, down 1.6 percent over the last month, which signals that dry powder is being deployed but not at a pace that suggests capitulation buying. Over the past four weekly periods, whale net flows swung from plus 903 million to minus 96 million to minus 126 million and back to plus 953 million. That volatility itself is the signal: major players are rotating, not committed to a single direction. The tactical redeployment of stablecoins onto exchanges suggests they are preparing for volatility, not announcing a bottom.

Sentiment stands at 28 on the Fear and Greed index, in the Fear zone and near the low of the 30-day range (which bottomed at 11). The crowd is genuinely worried. Yet the tape does not match that worry with capitulation. ETF flows tell a similar story: Bitcoin saw plus 32.1 million dollars on July 29 but is down 494 million over the last five sessions, same directional days only one. Ethereum is negative on the day at minus 32.9 million and down 56.2 million over five sessions. Traditional finance is pulling back, which is consistent with fear, but not fleeing. The modest uptick in BTC and DOGE MACD divergence combined with heavy short liquidations in a fearful sentiment environment creates asymmetry worth watching: if the bid holds here, the shorts are wrong. If it breaks, the longs are trapped.

Watch for a reclaim of the 200-day moving average by Bitcoin (the first real test of whether this regime holds) or a sharp reversal in the short liquidation flow (which would signal longs are being flushed). Monitor whether stablecoin reserves hold above 300 billion or decline further, as that figure marks the dry powder available for bids into weakness. The whale flow will remain volatile; what matters is whether the weekly net returns to sustained positive territory, signaling real institutional accumulation, or rolls back into the red. For now, the tape shows a market too tired to crash hard and not confident enough to rally.
